skill.name: azure-quotas
skill.description: Plan and manage Azure quota capacity with Azure CLI guidance, regional comparisons, quota increase workflows, and troubleshooting for service limits.
skill.summary: Check Azure quota limits, usage, regional capacity, and quota increase paths.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: The static detections are documentation-oriented false positives involving Markdown backticks, Azure CLI examples, and Microsoft links. I found one semantic risk: some workflows can change Azure subscription quota or provider registration state. No prompt injection or exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Quota update and provider registration commands can change Azure subscription state.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before running them, and show subscription, region, resource name, and requested limit first.

remediation.issue: Shell examples use values that may come from user input.
remediation.suggestion: Validate subscription IDs, providers, resource names, regions, and numeric limits before composing Azure CLI commands.

semantic_findings.title: Cloud Quota Changes Need Authorization
semantic_findings.description: The skill includes quota increase and provider registration guidance that can change Azure subscription state. Agents should require explicit user approval before running these commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines document az quota update and az provider register operations. These are legitimate tasks, but they can affect a real Azure subscription.

content.value_statement: Azure quota limits can block deployments and make region selection difficult. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through quota checks, usage review, increase requests, and fallback documentation.
actual_capabilities: Guides discovery of quota resource names with Azure CLI quota list workflows.
Shows how to review quota limits and current usage for supported Azure providers.
Explains regional quota comparison for deployment capacity planning.
Documents quota increase requests and request status checks.
Maps common Azure quota errors to troubleshooting actions.
Points to Microsoft Learn fallback documentation for unsupported providers.
limitations: Requires an authenticated Azure CLI session and appropriate Azure subscription permissions.
Does not verify live quota data unless commands run in the user environment.
Some Azure providers are not supported by the quota API.
Quota increase approval timing depends on Azure policy and capacity.

use_cases.title: Validate Deployment Capacity
use_cases.description: Check quota limits and usage before deploying virtual machines, networks, storage, or container resources.

use_cases.title: Resolve Quota Errors
use_cases.description: Diagnose quota exceeded failures and decide whether to request an increase or choose another region.

use_cases.title: Standardize Quota Requests
use_cases.description: Prepare repeatable quota review and increase workflows for teams managing shared Azure subscriptions.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Quota
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner quota lookup for one provider and region.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the azure-quotas skill to check my current quota and usage for Microsoft.Compute DSv3 vCPUs in eastus.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Regions
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare available quota for the same VM family across eastus, eastus2, westus2, and centralus. Recommend the best region.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose QuotaExceeded
prompt_templates.prompt: My Azure deployment failed with QuotaExceeded. Help me identify the relevant quota, current usage, available capacity, and next action.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Increase Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced quota increase planning with approval controls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a quota increase plan for a production deployment. Include checks, required permissions, confirmation steps, and fallback documentation.

output_examples.input: Check DSv3 vCPU capacity in eastus before a deployment that needs 80 more vCPUs.
output: Identifies the DSv3 quota resource name to inspect.
Reports current limit, current usage, and available capacity.
States whether the deployment fits and whether a quota increase is needed.

output_examples.input: Find a region with enough public IP quota for a new environment.
output: Compares candidate regions using the network quota provider.
Highlights regions with enough remaining public IP capacity.
Notes unsupported or incomplete provider responses and suggests documentation fallback.

output_examples.input: Prepare a safe quota increase request for a VM family.
output: Summarizes the current quota gap and requested target limit.
Lists required permission and confirmation details.
Explains how to track approval status after submission.

best_practices: Run quota discovery before checking a specific quota resource name.
Confirm subscription, provider, region, and requested limit before any quota change.
Compare regions early when capacity is flexible.
anti_patterns: Assuming REST API No Limit responses mean unlimited capacity.
Requesting quota increases without confirming the business need and scope.
Using ARM resource type names as quota resource names without discovery.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps check Azure quota limits, current usage, regional capacity, and quota increase workflows.

faq.question: Does it run Azure commands automatically?
faq.answer: It provides command guidance. Any command that changes Azure state should require explicit user approval.

faq.question: Which Azure tool does it prefer?
faq.answer: It prefers Azure CLI quota commands because the skill documentation treats them as the most reliable source.

faq.question: Can it request quota increases?
faq.answer: It explains the quota increase workflow, but users must authorize any request that changes a subscription.

faq.question: What permissions are needed?
faq.answer: Reader access is enough for viewing. Managing quotas needs quota request permissions or an equivalent role.

faq.question: What if a provider is unsupported?
faq.answer: The skill points users to Microsoft Learn, Azure Portal, or service-specific documentation for unsupported providers.
